results.observation: Looked for thin walls, shells, or membrane features. Front and right edge-on views show a solid, uniformly-filled rectangular cross-section (a solid disc seen on edge), not a hollow shell. Top and iso views show a solid spur-gear body: solid rim carrying the teeth, solid web between the central bore and the rim, no shelled cavities. No thin-wall or membrane geometry present; all sections are bulk solid, comfortably above the 0.8mm FDM floor.

results.rule_description: Overhang angle should not exceed 45 degrees from vertical without support
results.observation: Looked for overhangs, bridges, and away-from-vertical surfaces. In the standard flat-on-plate print orientation for a spur gear, the two large faces are flat (parallel to the build plate), the tooth flanks are vertical extrusions (self-supporting), and the central bore is an axial through-hole running in the build direction (a vertical hole, self-supporting). No surfaces angled beyond 45deg from vertical are visible. Note: the bore rims are not perfectly concentric in the top view (see PROPOSED-3DP-001) — if that reflects a tilted bore rather than a render artifact, the hole's upper side would become an overhang; verdict assumes an axial bore.

results.rule_description: Minimum feature size >= 0.5mm for reliable printing
results.observation: Looked for small protrusions, thin pins, text, and fine detail. The smallest repeated features are the gear teeth (~30 around the perimeter). In the top and iso views the teeth read as substantial, blocky features with clear width at both root and tip — not hair-thin pins or knife-edges. Tooth tips and roots appear well above the 0.5mm reliability floor relative to the overall part scale. No sub-0.5mm detail features (embossed text, fine ribs) present.

results.rule_description: All features must have adequate clearance for manufacturing tool access
results.observation: Looked for recessed features, internal cavities, and deep unreachable pockets. For an additive (3D printing) process there is no cutting-tool reach constraint — every surface is built up layer by layer. All features here (external teeth, flat faces, single central through-bore) are open and externally accessible with no enclosed voids or trapped internal cavities. Fully manufacturable additively.

results.rule_description: Prefer symmetric features to reduce setup operations and fixturing complexity
results.observation: Looked for overall symmetry and feature-placement patterns. The part is a spur gear: rotationally symmetric about its axis with a regular repeating tooth pattern and a centered through-bore. This is near-ideal symmetry, requiring no special fixturing or multi-setup handling.

results.rule_description: Horizontal holes should use a teardrop profile to prevent sagging at the top of the hole.
results.observation: Looked for horizontal circular holes that would sag. The only hole is the central bore. In the standard flat print orientation the bore is axial/vertical, so the teardrop rule would not apply. However, the top clean view shows the bore as two non-concentric rims (a crescent), and the iso wireframe shows an offset dashed (hidden) circle beside the solid bore — consistent with either a slightly tilted/non-axial bore or a rendering artifact. If the bore is genuinely tilted toward horizontal it could sag on its upper side.
results.recommendation: Confirm the bore is a straight axial through-hole concentric on both faces (inspect the CadQuery bore cut / part.py). If the gear is intended to print on-edge (bore horizontal), apply a teardrop profile to the bore. If printed flat with an axial bore, no action needed.

proposed_rules.description: A part's central/through bore must be concentric and axially aligned on both faces (rims coincident in the axial view).
proposed_rules.look_for: In the axial (top) orthographic view, the near and far rims of a through-bore should render as a single concentric circle; a crescent or offset inner circle indicates a tilted or non-concentric bore.
proposed_rules.pass_criteria: Both bore rims are concentric in the axial view; hidden-line rim coincides with visible rim.
proposed_rules.fail_criteria: Bore rims are laterally offset (crescent in the axial clean view, or an offset dashed rim in wireframe), indicating a skewed/non-axial or non-concentric bore.
